senses.gloss:
Kautasta, a word occurring once in the dual, is apparently
a patronymic of Arimejaya and Janamejaya, two Adhvaryu
priests at the snake sacrifice described in the Pañcaviṃśa
Brāhmaṇa.^1
1) xxv. 15, 3. Cf. Weber, Indische Studien, 1, 35.

Kautsa (‘descendant of Kutsa’) is mentioned in the Śata-
patha Brāhmaṇa^1 as a pupil of Māhitthi. A Kautsa is also
attacked in the Nirukta^2 as denying the value of the Vedas, and
there is a strong ritual tradition of hostility to the Kautsas.^3
1) x. 6, 5, 9; Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upani-
ṣad, vi. 5, 4 (Kāṇva recension only).
2) i. 15.
3) E.g., Āpastamba Śrauta Sūtra,
x. 20, 12; Hillebrandt, Vedische Myth-
ologie, 3, 285. Cf. Weber, Indian
Literature, 77, 140.

Kautsī-putra (‘son of a female descendant of Kutsa’) is
mentioned as a pupil of Baudhīputra in the last Vaṃśa
(list of teachers) of the Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad in the
Mādhyaṃdina recension (vi. 4, 31).
